2 — How C reaches Lisp: two mechanisms, on purpose
libusb has four callback types. They are not the same problem, so they are not solved the same way.
dispatched on a Lisp event-pump thread (:thread) or on the thread that is waiting for a transfer (:manual)
the only native callback in the image
a libffi closure per Lisp closure
the closure carries its own Lisp state
mirror status and actual_length into Lisp
run the user function — which may resubmit
set the completion flag, then signal the semaphore
log: (ctx level message), with a reentrancy guard
Why not one mechanism for both:
a libffi closure costs an mmap'd executable page, and transfers are many and short-lived — struct libusb_transfer hands us a void* that is exactly the demultiplexer a closure
would pay for. Meanwhile libusb_set_log_cb takes no user_data at all, so a per-context Lisp handler has nowhere to put an index and must BE its own C function pointer.
